title: Which party will win the Holborn and St Pancras by-election?
resolution_criteria: This question will resolve as the political party of the candidate officially declared elected as Member of Parliament for the Holborn and St Pancras constituency in the 2026 by-election.
fine_print:
* If a candidate of a party not listed, or an independent candidate wins, the question will resolve as Other.
* If a candidate changes party affiliation after nominations close but before taking their seat, the party listed on the official election result will determine resolution.
* If the by-election is cancelled because of a general election, constituency abolition, or another electoral event that prevents the by-election from taking place, the question will be annulled.
background:
A by-election is due to take place in [Holborn and St Pancras](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2026_Holborn_and_St_Pancras_by-election) following the resignation of former Prime Minister Keir Starmer from the House of Commons on 1 September 2026.

The constituency is an inner London seat covering parts of the London Borough of Camden. At the 2024 general election, Labour won the seat with 48.9% of the vote, although its vote share fell substantially compared with the previous election. Independent candidate Andrew Feinstein finished second with 18.9%, while the Green Party finished third on 10.4%.

Labour [has selected](https://www.standard.co.uk/news/politics/sagal-abdiwali-labour-favourite-holborn-byelection-keir-starmer-b1296058.html) councillor Sagal Abdi-Wali to be their candidate.

The Green Party has attracted particular attention ahead of the by-election. Party members [have backed](https://www.theguardian.com/politics/2026/sep/11/zack-polanski-selected-green-party-holborn-st-pancras-byelection) their leader, Zack Polanski, to seek the party's nomination.

comments.author: DaiLothbrook
comments.text: I keep my bet mostly on Labour at 86%, close to the original 85% baseline, because its official [\[2024 ](https://news.camden.gov.uk/general-election-results/)majority was 11,572 votes, its candidate leads Camden Council, and the latest [\[bookmaker comparison   ](https://www.oddschecker.com/insight/politics/20260921-holborn-st-pancras-by-election-odds-labour-odds-shorten)  makes Labour an overwhelming favourite. I nevertheless raise the Greens from 5% to 13% because Zack Polanski is a national party leader and the reported May 2026 ward results reduced Labour’s local lead over the Greens to roughly ten points; most of that gain comes from collapsing Other rather than sharply downgrading Labour, since the left-wing independent who finished second in 2024  might not be the principal challenger in this contest.Anyway, I am not a specialist in british politics, that has its many particularities, That is not necessarily easy to follow.

comments.author: sai_39
comments.text: [PollCheck's](https://www.pollcheck.co.uk/by-elections/holborn-and-st-pancras) by-election model has Labour first and Green second, on 41.7% and 37.8%, a margin of 3.9 points. Across 10,000 simulations Labour win 70% of the time. 1\) Zack Polanski has consolidated much of the progressive opposition. Andrew Feinstein, who received \~19% as an independent in 2024, is not standing and has endorsed Polanski. The Greens themselves received more than 10% in 2024. Those votes are not mechanically additive, but the endorsement makes the Green challenge credible. [Reuters](https://www.reuters.com/world/uk-green-leader-confirmed-candidate-parliament-seat-vacated-by-starmer-2026-09-11/) 2\) Labour selected Sagal Abdi-Wali, Camden Council’s local leader. Her borough roots and Somali-refugee background make her a considerably stronger candidate here than a national figure would have been. [The Times](https://www.thetimes.com/uk/politics/article/the-childhood-refugee-fighting-zack-polanski-for-starmers-seat-0mj9zss68) 3\)George Galloway is standing for the Workers Party. He could take some Gaza-focused and anti-Labour voters who might otherwise consolidate behind Polanski. That is probably worth a few percentage points to Labour’s winning chances. [Novaramedia](https://novaramedia.com/2026/09/14/george-galloway-to-stand-in-byelection-in-attempt-to-defeat-green-leader/) 4\) A small operational setback for the Greens: their annual conference runs from 2–4 October, consuming activists and attention immediately before polling day. Polanski reportedly wanted it postponed, but the party executive refused. [The Guardian](https://www.theguardian.com/politics/2026/sep/18/zack-polanski-request-postpone-greens-conference-byelection-refused) I think Polanski as the only plausible upset winner. This [wikipedia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2026_Holborn_and_St_Pancras_by-election) page was useful to get some context.

comments.author: matru
re73
comments.text: The Greens' principal advantage in the first half of 2026 was that they framed their party as a mostly urban progressive anti-Starmer organisation. Starmer is gone, and Labour's new leader Andy Burnham is very acceptable to urban progressives on a whole host of issues (Gaza, electoral reform, devolution, etc.). Labour had a notional advantage in H\&StP anyway on UNS polling, and I think the demography of the seat makes it likely Labour will retain it

comments.author: Koboh
comments.text:
**My prediction: Labour 76%, Green 23%, Other 1%.**

I’m backing Labour here, but I don’t think this is anywhere near as comfortable as the 2024 result suggests. Labour’s long standing strength in Holborn & St Pancras and Sagal Abdi-Wali’s strong local profile give them the advantage, but the Greens have made a real breakthrough in Camden. The key factor is whether Zack Polanski can consolidate the progressive vote that previously went to Andrew Feinstein, who is now standing aside and backing the Greens. The May local election results show that Labour’s lead has narrowed considerably, so a Green upset is absolutely possible.

[https://polymarket.com/event/holborn-and-st-pancras-by-election-winner](https://polymarket.com/event/holborn-and-st-pancras-by-election-winner)

 I think Labour’s organisation, local base and broader vote make them the more likely winner. I’d put Labour at around 76%, Greens 23%, and everyone else collectively around 1%. No constituency poll has been published yet, so I’d keep some uncertainty around that estimate.

[https://www.pollcheck.co.uk/by-elections/holborn-and-st-pancras](https://www.pollcheck.co.uk/by-elections/holborn-and-st-pancras)

comments.author: GOLDEN-BLUE
comments.text: Labour won by \~6% over the Greens in the local elections (the borough is a bit bigger than the constituency) however since the locals Labour has rebounded in the polls and the Greens have collapsed. Bookies will give you 3/1 for the Greens and 3/10 for Labour.
